mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC mobility has shown a general upward trend (less negative) from t-3w to t-1w, suggesting a slow but steady return to baseline activity. This underlying momentum is expected to continue, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES mobility from t-1w (-22.7) to t-0w (-3.4) indicates the end of a holiday period and a strong return to normal work patterns. This increased presence in workplaces will drive associated retail and recreation spending during weekdays, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following a week-on-week WORKPLACES rebound of more than 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: The recent dip in PARKS mobility at t-0w, following a strong increase, combined with a dip in RESIDENTIAL mobility, suggests a temporary weather-related setback. As spring progresses, improved weather will drive both PARKS and RETAIL_REC higher, as people spend more time outdoors and in associated retail areas over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to decline or stagnate, and RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks despite seasonal expectations.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained significantly below baseline, indicating persistent reluctance for public transport use. If TRANSIT mobility continues to hover around -15% or drops further, it will negatively impact footfall in retail and recreation areas heavily reliant on transit access, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -10% for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has consistently remained elevated above baseline, indicating that a significant portion of the population continues to spend more time at home. This sustained higher residential presence will continue to suppress out-of-home retail and recreation activities, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below +5% for two consecutive weeks, and RETAIL_REC increases over the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The recent dip in GROCERY_PHARM mobility at t-0w, combined with the strong recovery in WORKPLACES, suggests a shift from essential local errands back to work-related commuting patterns. This shift implies less local neighborhood retail and more activity near workplaces, which could boost RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM drops while WORKPLACES rises week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in the week following a simultaneous drop in GROCERY_PHARM and rise in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: Given the overall negative mobility indices, the metropolitan area is likely in a cautious reopening or recovery phase. In this regime, any sustained improvement in PARKS mobility (indicating growing comfort with outdoor public spaces) will precede and encourage a gradual increase in RETAIL_REC as public confidence grows over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility shows a positive trend over two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility improves for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility sustains its recovery from the t-1w dip and remains above -5% for two consecutive weeks, it signals a stable return to office-based work. This sustained presence will provide a consistent boost to RETAIL_REC, particularly for businesses catering to office workers, over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains above -5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES remains above -5% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC declines over the subsequent two weeks.
